{{Quote|Bohhuah Mutdah is a retired industrialist, a trillionaire. His holdings in the Oseon are the largest in the system by a single individual, and it is possible that he is the wealthiest person in the civilized galaxy. He is also thoroughly addicted to ''lesai''.|[[Waywa Fybot]]|<ref name="LCFO" />}}
'''Bohhuah Mutdah''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] industrialist who by the early [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]] had amassed one of the largest fortunes in the known [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. Mutdah achieved incredible reaches through the diligent application of his formidable intellect and his addiction to ''[[Lesai/Legends|lesai]]'', a narcotic that allowed him to forgo sleep entirely. The largest private landowner in the [[Oseon system/Legends|Oseon system]], Mutdah retired to his estate on [[Oseon 5792]], before being [[Death/Legends|murdered]] in [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]] by [[Sorcerers of Tund/Legends|Sorcerer of Tund]] [[Rokur Gepta]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|What have you people got against this Mutdah character&mdash;or is it simply that you don't like the size of his bank account?|Lando Calrissian|<ref name="LCFO" />}}
Over 100 years old by [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]]&mdash;a longevity due in part to the [[Rafa system/Legends|Rafa]] [[life-crystal]] he wore around his neck&mdash;<ref name="cswe">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> Bohhuah Mutdah was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] businessman who saw tremendous success in the latter years of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] into the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]]. Although coming from relatively humble beginnings, Mutdah earned an incredible fortune as an industrialist, becoming the single largest private landowner in the wealthy [[Oseon system/Legends|Oseon system]]. By 3 BBY, there were some who believed that he might have been the single wealthiest being in the known [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="LCFO" />

Mutdah's success was at least partly attributed to his addiction to the drug ''[[Lesai/Legends|lesai]]'', which eliminated the necessity for sleep and allowed Mutdah to spend even more time preparing to crush his competition. Mutdah had retired by 3 BBY, moving into a massive, palatial estate on [[Oseon 5792]] and spending the days indulging his basest instincts in a never-ending search for any kind of feeling. Mutdah spent decades in apathetic leisure, growing enormously obese over time and regularly receiving offworld ''lesai'' shipments. Mutdah's extended retirement ended in 3 BBY, when [[Sorcerers of Tund/Legends|Sorcerer of Tund]] [[Rokur Gepta]] [[Death/Legends|murdered]] him to assume his identity in a scheme to entrap [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]].<ref name="LCFO" />

==Personality and traits==
An incredibly intelligent Human who once diligently applied his intellect to becoming one of the richest beings in the galaxy, Mutdah descended into a life of complete hedonism and indolence after retiring to his Oseon estate. Already a large man, Mutdah's sedentary, indulgent lifestyle led to him gaining a tremendous amount of weight, reaching between 300 and 350 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]] on his two-plus [[Meter/Legends|meter]] frame. Mutdah hardly moved physically at all in his later years, spending his days sitting in a gel-filled recliner within a protective force field. By 3 BBY, he had not entered a standard gravitic field for 25 years, and had not used his own two hands for anything in five years.<ref name="LCFO" />

Mutdah was a ''lesai'' addict, which became a crucial part of his success in business&mdash;the elimination of his need to sleep allowed him the little extra advantage he needed to dominate the competition, and allowed him even more time to apply his tremendous intellect. Beyond that, Mutdah saw his ''lesai'' addiction as his reason to live in his later years. Mutdah had achieved incredible wealth, but found that nothing interested him or triggered any emotion except the drug. In fact, he found that he had no true will to live&mdash;rather, he persisted out of sheer apathetic inertia, completely uncaring about anything he encountered. Mutdah did enjoy literature on some level, as he had a notably large and diverse library on his estate and employed a [[Ekisp|servant]] to read to him.<ref name="LCFO" />

==Behind the scenes==
Bohhuah Mutdah appeared in ''[[Lando Calrissian and the Flamewind of Oseon]]'', written by [[L. Neil Smith]] and released in [[1983]].<ref name="LCFO" />
